_schema: testId, environment, timestampUtc, machineId, softwareVersion, gitCommit, procedure, expectedResult, observedResult, status (PASS|FAIL|BLOCKED|NOT_VERIFIED|NOT_APPLICABLE), evidenceRef, operatorNotes

records.machineId: build-container (this Linux/container environment - NOT the HP EliteBook 830 G6 pilot machine)
records.procedure: rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-gnu; apt-get install mingw-w64 nsis; cargo tauri build --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --bundles nsis, with CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_PC_WINDOWS_GNU_LINKER=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc
records.expectedResult: a real PE32+ Windows x64 executable and NSIS .exe installer are produced without fabricating either
records.observedResult: cip-desktop.exe built successfully (PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64, stripped to external PDB, for MS Windows, 11 sections, confirmed via `file`); see release/release-manifest-3.4.json for the bundled installer result and checksum
records.operatorNotes: This is Environment A/B cross-compilation evidence only - it proves the toolchain produces a well-formed Windows PE binary and NSIS installer from this Linux container. It is NOT evidence the installer runs, installs, or launches on a real Windows machine - no Wine, no Windows VM, and no WebView2 runtime exist in this container to test that. See WIN-INSTALL-02 through WIN-INSTALL-07 below.

records.procedure: Copy the .exe installer to the HP EliteBook 830 G6 (or equivalent Windows 11 machine). Double-click to run it. Confirm no admin/Git/Rust/Node/dev-tool prompt appears beyond normal Windows installer/UAC behavior.
records.expectedResult: Installer runs to completion using only the standard Windows installer UI
records.operatorNotes: No Windows machine available in this container. See docs/phase-3-4-windows-pilot.md section F for the exact operator procedure.

records.procedure: Launch CIP from the Start Menu / desktop shortcut the installer created.
records.expectedResult: Application window opens, no crash, no missing-DLL error

records.procedure: Exit the application via its normal close control.
records.expectedResult: Clean exit, no error dialog, process fully terminates

records.procedure: Re-launch the application a second time.
records.expectedResult: Application opens normally, database/BSB dataset already present from first launch (0 re-import), no duplicate data

records.procedure: Uninstall CIP via Windows Settings > Apps, or the NSIS uninstaller shortcut.
records.expectedResult: Application and its Start Menu entries are removed cleanly
records.operatorNotes: Whether user data (%APPDATA%) is retained or removed on uninstall should be recorded, not assumed.
